regulations.name: ASTM E 1965-98(2016) - Standard Specification for Infrared Thermometers for Intermittent Determination of Patient Temperature

requirements.description: The following requirements shall apply to any IR thermometer that is labeled to meet these specifications.
Displayed Temperature Range
In any display mode, an ear canal IR thermometer shall display a subject's temperature over a minimum range of 34.4 to 42.2 °C (94.0 to 108.0 °F).
A skin IR thermometer shall display a subject's temperature over a minimum range of 22 to 40.0 °C (71.6 to 104.0 °F).
Maximum Permissible Laboratory Error (for an Ear Canal IR Thermometer)
Within the manufacturer's specified operating ambient conditions (see 5.6), laboratory error δ as measured according to 6.1.4 shall be no greater than values specified below.
For blackbody temperature range from 36 to 39 °C (96.8 to 102.2 °F): 0.2 °C (0.4 °F).
For blackbody temperatures less than 36 °C (96.8 °F) or greater than 39 °C (102.2 °F): 0.3 °C (0.5 °F).
Maximum Permissible Laboratory Error (for a Skin IR Thermometer)

Within the manufacturer's specified operating ambient conditions (see 5.6) over the display temperature range as specified in 5.2.2, laboratory error δ as measured according to 6.1.5 shall be no greater than 0.3 °C (0.5 °F).
Special Requirements
Clinical Accuracy
The clinical accuracy requirement is applicable only to an ear canal IR thermometer system and the corresponding age groups of subjects for which such a thermometer is labeled or implied to be used.

Clinical accuracy shall be determined separately for each of the following conditions: for each device model, for each adjusted display mode, and for every age group of febrile and afebrile subjects on which the IR thermometer is intended to be used.
requirements.result_remark: Clinical accuracy is not evaluated in this report.

requirements.description: Any disclosure of clinical accuracy claims shall be accompanied by disclosure of methodology and procedures. Such information shall be made available on request.
Clinical accuracy should be determined in the form of two characteristics — clinical bias with stated uncertainty and clinical repeatability, as defined in 3.2.9.
Ambient Conditions
Operating Temperature Range
The system shall meet laboratory error requirements as specified in 5.3 or 5.4, or both, when operating in an environment from 16 to 40 °C (60.8 to 104.0 °F).
If the operating temperature range is narrower than specified in 5.6.1.1, the device shall be clearly labeled with a cautionary statement of the maximum or minimum operating temperatures, or both.
Under no circumstances may the upper limit of operating temperature range be less than 35 °C (95 °F).
Operating Humidity Range — The relative humidity range for the operating temperature range as specified in 5.6.1 is up to 95%, noncondensing.
Shock

The instrument with batteries installed (if applicable) without a carrying (storage) casing shall withstand drops with controlled orientation of the device without degradation of accuracy as specified in 5.3 or 5.4, or both, for a blackbody temperature of or near 37 °C (98.6 °F), when tested according to 6.3.
If an IR thermometer does not meet the requirement of 5.6.3.1, a means of detecting and informing the user of its inoperable state, after being subjected to shock, shall be provided.

Storage Conditions — The instrument shall meet the accuracy requirements of 5.3 or 5.4, or both, after having been stored or transported, or both, at any point in an environment of –20 to +50 °C (–4 to +122 °F) and relative humidity up to 95%, noncondensing, for a period of one month. The test procedure is specified in 6.1.6.

semantic_fragments.content: Clinical accuracy is not evaluated in this report. Clinical accuracy shall be determined separately for each device model, for each adjusted display mode, and for every age group of febrile and afebrile subjects on which the IR thermometer is intended to be used. Any disclosure of clinical accuracy claims shall be accompanied by disclosure of methodology and procedures. Clinical accuracy should be determined in the form of two characteristics — clinical bias with stated uncertainty and clinical repeatability.

The device under test has no ear canal mode (5.2.1, 5.3, 5.3.1.1, 5.3.1.2 are all N/A). The device operates as a skin/forehead IR thermometer only, with a display range of 32°C ~ 43°C in forehead (FA) mode.

The operating temperature range of the device is 10°C - 40°C, which is narrower than the standard-specified range of 16 to 40°C for the laboratory error test but meets the requirement that the upper limit shall not be less than 35°C. Because the range is narrower than the standard specification of 5.6.1.1, clause 5.6.1.2 applies and the device shall be clearly labeled with cautionary statements regarding operating temperature limits.

Storage Conditions: The instrument shall meet the accuracy requirements after having been stored or transported at any point in an environment of –20 to +50°C and relative humidity up to 95%, noncondensing, for a period of one month. Results recorded in TABLE 5.6.4 with verdict P (Pass).
